correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RKHS Gram projection and confirmed exact tensor kernel mean g=diag(K)/2^d. One-axis factorization and the three-interval bridge residual establish the unique trisection/midpoint optimum and exact weights. A one-variable derivative with strictly decreasing numerator proves the unique mirrored optimum; strict convexity of log cosh proves increasing normalized captured energy; a constructive log-separation limit establishes 27/16; the root equation gives the Lambert W separation. The actual standalone package verifier passed 379 exact rational identities and 150 numerical root/trend spot checks; they supplement rather than replace the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The exact original object is two optimally weighted point evaluations of the integration functional on a d-fold anchored mixed-Sobolev kernel. The 2017 random-node paper concerns convergence-rate constants; the 2018 tensor-kernel paper provides a kernel and worst-case-error method but not the present sharp two-point design-class comparison; the 2022 Brownian-bridge paper treats 1D supremum interpolation power, not d-dimensional integral risk. Targeted scientific matching identified no dominating theorem in inspected relevant material; historical priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: Classical spline-cubature and mixed-smoothness literature beyond the inspected primary sources may encode the same two-node design comparison under an equivalent norm.
The theorem optimizes only the two named design classes; an unrestricted pair might do better.
The asymptotic advantage is for captured integration representer energy, whose fraction of total energy vanishes exponentially in dimension.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial two-point budget in a d-dimensional anchored mixed-Sobolev cubature problem is a natural sharp finite-sample benchmark. The theorem classifies every one-axis optimum, constructs a unique superior reflected-diagonal rule for every d>=2 and proves a strict increasing all-dimension energy advantage with limiting factor 27/16. This supplies a structurally motivated boundary for single-axis sparse refinements. The relative total-error benefit may be small in high dimension; no practical speedup or unrestricted optimum is claimed.
